mutants.description: Rhie--Chow damping enters the face flux with the wrong sign
mutants.rationale: The damping term is what prevents checkerboard pressure/velocity decoupling on collocated grids; flipping it must move the steady solution or destroy convergence.

mutants.description: Non-orthogonal cross term dropped from the face normal pressure
mutants.rationale: On skewed body-fitted cells the projected-gradient correction carries the tangential part of the pressure gradient into the face flux.  If no test varies skewness, the deletion survives and the suite only certifies orthogonal-grid behaviour.

mutants.description: Pseudo-time damping ratio inverted (steady_df/df instead of df/steady_df)
mutants.rationale: beta blends the retained face-flux memory with the unrelaxed operator; inverting the ratio selects the complementary blend, so the pseudo-time and velocity-relaxation equivalence tests must fail.

mutants.description: Projected-linear face weights applied to the wrong owner/neighbour
mutants.rationale: Swapping the bracket keeps the weights admissible, so the existing bracketing guard cannot catch it; only a test that compares the interpolated face value against the exact linear field on a stretched grid can.

mutants.description: Outlet faces no longer zeroed in the Gauss pressure gradient
mutants.rationale: The gauge of a pressure gradient with a prescribed outlet pressure depends on this masking; a suite that only checks force balance can let it through.

mutants.description: Staggered u-face interpolation replaced by first-order upwind
mutants.rationale: Upwinding biases every face value, so the channel-profile refinement test and the steady-state equivalence tests should react; if tolerances are loose enough it survives.
